title: Investigate partial ingestion duplication causing cross-deploy billing mismatches
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported apparent duplicate token charges across Hosted and Dedicated environments after regional failover events. Initial triage shows a narrow window where ingestion from the message bus was partially duplicated and downstream accounting services did not collapse duplicates consistently across deployments (hosted pool vs dedicated pool). This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and permanent fixes to prevent re-occurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Trigger regional failover simulating node termination in Dedicated pool (scale down + promote fallback)
2) Replay a mix of client requests containing idempotency keys and short-lived sessions through the ingress router
3) Simultaneously enable a small downstream replay from the ingestion topic (manual offset rewind by 1-2k messages)
4) Observe accounting service ingestion and aggregation, specifically the EventCollector -> HourlyAggregator -> ChargeMerger path
observed_symptoms: - Duplicate token increments appearing in hourly aggregation for affected customers (5% of tokens in window)
- Discrepancy between real-time stream counts and final invoice counts after merge job (delta ~ +12k tokens)
- Inconsistent dedup behavior between Hosted (ingest dedup window = 2s) and Dedicated (ephemeral idempotency cache expired immediately after failover)
- KV-cache state divergence observed on resumed Dedicated nodes causing repeated cache-miss billing increments
diagnosis: - Root cause is a race during failover where ingress retries + manual replay created overlapping messages with identical client-side idempotency keys
- Dedicated nodes were running a short-lived in-memory idempotency cache (TTL = 1s) that did not persist across node termination, so replays after failover produced new accounting events

- Hourly aggregation job (ChargeMerger) assumes upstream deduplication guarantees and performs a loose merge keyed on (customer, minute) which collapsed some duplicates but left partial duplicates unmerged
- Message bus (Kafka) compacted topics but our consumer group offsets were manipulated during incident causing duplicate consumption across two consumer group instances
mitigation: - Hotfix: temporarily enable request-level dedup at the Accounting API (persistent Redis dedup store with 1h TTL) to collapse immediate duplicate increments
- Re-run deterministic merge job for affected hourly windows (2026-03-09T03:00Z to 2026-03-09T06:00Z) using strict idempotency-key matching
- Notified impacted customers via CS and issued provisional billing credits while we complete the root-cause fix
- Enabled additional tracing at ingress and accounting to capture idempotency keys and consumer offsets for next 72 hours
unresolved_risks: - Potential edge cases where clients do not provide idempotency keys (legacy SDKs) — those requests may still double-count without additional safeguards
- Performance impact of persistent Redis dedup store under peak load if kept long-term
- Race remains for very short windows if node termination and replay overlap and dedup info is not propagated quickly
permanent_fixes_proposed: 1) Implement distributed idempotency: write-through idempotency store in Durable Metadata Service (stable across failovers) with best-effort async TTL cleanup
2) Harden ChargeMerger: switch from minute-level loose merge to idempotency-key-first merge when keys present; fallback to existing strategy when absent
3) Update Dedicated agent to persist transient idempotency cache to local durable store on graceful shutdown; add on-start reconciliation to consume last-seen idempotency windows
4) Improve consumer group failover handling: avoid manual offset manipulations; build automatic offset reconcile tool to detect duplicate consumption
5) Add canary and synthetic tests that simulate rapid failover + replay to validate dedup guarantees across Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes
next_steps: - E/N: finalize hotfix rollback plan and monitor Redis dedup hit-rate (ETA 2026-03-12)
- SRE: schedule deterministic merge run for affected windows and verify invoice delta (ETA 2026-03-13)
- Platform: design API and schema changes for distributed idempotency store; draft RFC (owner: Priya Rao, due 2026-03-20)
- QA: create a failure-injection test harness for failover+replay scenarios and add to Cycle 2026-W11
